newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-PORTUGUESA REACH BRAZIL FINAL FOR FIRST TIME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTUGUESA REACH BRAZIL FINAL FOR FIRST TIME.

text.p: Portuguesa reached the Brazilian championship final for the first time on Sunday but there was confusion over the dates for the most important domestic game of the season.

Portuguesa held on for a 2-2 draw at Atletico Mineiro in the second leg of their semifinal to win 3-2 on aggregate and will play Gremio who drew 2-2 at home to Goias but went through thanks to a 3-1 away win in midweek.
Portuguesa survived despite having to substitute their top player Rodrigo, who was forced off injured after suffering a battering from the Atletico defence.
Atletico, backed by an 81,000 crowd in Belo Horizonte, needed to win by one goal to qualify on having the better overall record in the competition.

Renaldo put Atletico ahead with a first half penalty, his 16th goal of the competition, but Portuguesa turned the game around with a penalty by Caio and a breakaway goal by Alex Alves in the second half.
Striker Euler set up a dramatic finale by equalising for Atletico, who had won all 12 previous home games in the tournament, in the 80th minute.
Gremio, 1995 South American champions, twice came from behind against Goias, who were aiming for their first final appearance.
The first leg of the final was originally due to be played either Wednesday or Thursday with the second match the following Sunday.
But confusion reigned after Gremio president Fabio Koff said on Sunday he had proposed the first leg should be switched to next Sunday with the decisive game on December 22.

It was also unclear as to where Portuguesa's home match would be staged as competition rules stipulate that final venues must have a minimum capacity of 40,000. No stadium in their home city of Sao Paulo can hold that many people.
To make the situation more bizarre, unfashionable Portuguesa's biggest home crowd this season was 21,000.
Brazil's football authorities are frequently criticised for chopping and changing venues and dates of games without prior warning.
The change would benefit Gremio, who have key defenders Catalino Rivarola and Francisco Arce playing in a World Cup qualifier for Paraguay next Sunday.
